doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Traveling with Dave and staying home
summary: Iola began traveling with Dave after the children grew; flying no longer fun, they prefer to stay home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And you weren’t really able to travel too much with Dave until the children got to be a certain age?

Yeah. Quite a bit older. Matthew, the youngest, went to boarding school at Choate so he was at that point I guess 14 or something like that. And after that I started, not all the time, but then in more recent years I’ve traveled with him all the time.
I know travel was difficult for him, and I wondered, do you like it?

It depends on where we’re going and how we get there. It’s difficult. I would say it’s no longer fun to get on an airplane and travel. And for a while Dave was saying, “Well we’ll just do stuff that we can drive to.” And that’s more or less what we’ve done more © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
recently. But I would say the excitement of leaving here and going someplace else is not what it used to be. I think we’re pretty happy just to be here.
It’s a good place to be.
